citeAs: Lu, W., Ye, M., Ye, Z., Tao, R., Yang, S., & Zhao, B. (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.12224.
creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xiamen University, Harbin Institute of Technology)
description: A large-scale dataset of robotic failures comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments.
name: RoboFAC dataset
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For five question types, reference answers were extracted directly from textual descriptions. For three complex question types, GPT-4o generated reference answers based on the video and text descriptions, which were then manually reviewed and corrected.
rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected in the ManiSkill environment using motion planning, with perturbations added to generate failures. Real-world data was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of robotic manipulation videos (simulation and real-world) and corresponding textual descriptions including the error substage, failure taxonomy, and perturbed pose.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Simulation environments were augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Perturbations were added to expert policies to generate erroneous trajectories.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual thorough data cleaning was performed, retaining approximately 75% of the collected data.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating multimodal models for robotic failure video understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.

null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Not applicable to robotic manipulation data.
null_reasons.rai:dataLimitations: The paper discusses model limitations, but not dataset limitations.
